subject: Weekly staff flashpoint: priorities & QBR asks
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly staff flashpoint: priorities & QBR asks

Team —

Quick weekly snapshot ahead of QBR prep. Keeping this tight: wins, near-term risks, and explicit asks (who/when). Attaching a one-pager for the QBR and the sprint metrics workbook.

Wins
- Redwood Dedicated pilot for Acme Analytics completed first full-week throughput test; sustained 4k rps equivalent during peak windows (see sprint sheet).
- Latency SLOs for small-batch chat improved after kernel update (p90 down ~18%).
- Two engineering hires in serving runtime onboarded last week; immediate impact on triage turnaround.

Risks / Issues
- Procurement: Acme is asking for an exception to our standard T&Cs (data residency clarifications). Sales is flagged and legal will need to review — timeline could slip for Dedicated contract signing (impact: revenue commit delayed ~2–3 weeks).
- Capacity: Dedicated cluster autoscale policy needs a conservative cap change to avoid CPU contention during multi-tenant benchmarks; ops will need a planned maintenance window to adjust.
- QBR narrative: we have mixed performance signals across regions; if we don’t reconcile the EU perf delta, exec narrative looks disjointed.

Asks (owner — due)
- Laura: Prioritize whether we surface the EU perf delta as an open action in the QBR or a mitigated risk. (Laura — EOD Thu)
- Marissa: Coordinate with Sales to capture Acme’s requested T&C changes and confirm whether we can accept a carve-out for data residency language. (Marissa — Tue 4/27)
- Jonas: Schedule a 60-min ops window next Tue to bump autoscale caps and run a stress pass; include rollback plan. (Jonas — schedule by Mon 4/26)
- Randy (Acme): Please confirm whether the residency carve-out would be a dealbreaker or negotiable; we can put a proposed language in the contract. (Randy — please reply)

Deliverables attached: qbr_priorities_onepager_v2.pdf (one-page narrative + key charts), sprint-metrics_20270421.xlsx (perf, infra spend, job traces).

I’ll consolidate replies into a QBR slide stub Friday morning.

Thanks —
Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Sr. Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Weekly staff flashpoint: priorities & QBR asks

Thanks Nikhil — good summary. Two clarifications before I decide on the EU framing: 
1) Can you add a one-line root-cause hypothesis for the EU perf delta on the one-pager (e.g., kernel mismatch vs routing)? I want to avoid a nebulous callout in the slides.
2) For Acme: is the requested carve-out limited to logs/retention or are they asking for broader data residency (processing and storage)? If it’s only logs, we have standard mitigations.

Make those updates and resend by EOD and I’ll signal whether we treat it as mitigated or open risk in the QBR narrative.

Laura Bennett
VP, Product
Redwood Inference

Laura — thanks. Updated one-pager attached: I added a one-line hypothesis under "EU perf delta" (likely routing + slightly older kernel on that pool; we’ll validate during the ops window). For Acme I confirmed with Sales: their primary ask is data residency for logs and audit artifacts for 12 months; they are not asking to restrict runtime processing. 

Actions taken
- Updated qbr_priorities_onepager_v2.pdf (section: EU perf delta — hypothesis + next test).
- Pushed sprint-metrics_20270421.xlsx with a new sheet that isolates EU cluster job traces.
- Tagged Randy on this thread for a direct yes/no on whether the log residency approach would be acceptable as a contractual carve-out.

Next steps
- Jonas: please still run the 60-min autoscale window Tue (Mon to schedule) — we need the stress pass for the slide chart.
- Marissa: if legal needs sample contract language, I can draft a proposed clause this afternoon for review.

Attachments: qbr_priorities_onepager_v2.pdf, sprint-metrics_20270421.xlsx

-Nikhil
